The .mjs extension selects ECMAScript module parsing in Node. An importer cannot reassign count. Adding count = 9 to main.mjs throws TypeError at execution, even though counter.mjs declared the exported binding with let. An ECMAScript module can export values for other files to import.

This lesson uses two local Node files. The `.mjs` extension tells Node to treat them as modules. Save them together in a new practice folder.

The in-app lesson teaches the example; it does not run these imports.

Save this beside it as `main.mjs`, then run `node main.mjs`.
```javascript
import { count, increment } from "./counter.mjs";
console.log(count);
console.log(increment());
console.log(count);
```
Output:
```text
0
1
1
```
The import stays connected to the exported count. It sees the update after `increment()` runs. The file path includes `./` and the `.mjs` extension.

The importing file can read `count`, but cannot assign a new value to that imported name. Adding `count = 9` in `main.mjs` would throw a TypeError.

Use the exported `increment` function to change the value. Calling it twice makes the next read of count return 2.

Completing the reading and quiz is separate from running the files locally.
